correctness.rationale: The maximal-face dichotomy is proved. On each star simplex, the explicit unique-maximum spoke retraction is continuous, equivariant, and fixes all overlaps, yielding a global strong equivariant deformation retraction. Each exceptional triangle attaches along a simple subdivided triangle loop; equivariant gluing gives the full 2-skeleton model for every m>=4. Integral oriented cellular 2-chains are exterior cubed of Z^m and the boundary is contraction by the augmentation, so the kernel is exactly exterior cubed of U_m. All higher homology vanishes. Exact mod-two Betti checks for m=4..7 and 864 signed character comparisons corroborate but do not supply the infinite/integral proof.

originality.rationale: Barmak 2010 proves the precise nonequivariant wedge count but not the equivariant homotopy model or integral module. The new proof supplies an explicit symmetric retraction and a canonical integral lattice isomorphism. Searches for exact aliases, stronger results, tables, and different Kneser functors returned no covering statement. Risk remains from unindexed implicit equivariant results; a published nonequivariant homotopy theorem alone does not imply the action classification.
residual_risks: An unindexed treatment may already give an equivariant simplex-skeleton model for these two-subset complexes.
The published Barmak simplex classification makes the equivariant refinement accessible, though it does not itself state or prove the equivariant homotopy claim.

value.rationale: This natural infinite family is a benchmark in Kneser-graph topological combinatorics. The known wedge count determines only ranks; the new explicit S_m-equivariant homotopy model and full integral exterior-power lattice determine every symmetry character and the integral action, with a uniform explanation by a fixed-point-compatible geometric retraction. It is not an arbitrary parameter slice or recomputation of the known rank.
